subject: religious-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which phrase from Genesis 2:24 is used by Christians to describe the union created by marriage?
questions.explain: Genesis 2:24 states that in marriage a man and woman are united and 'become one flesh'.

questions.q: Which teaching of Jesus (Mark 10:9) is often read at Christian weddings?
options: What God has joined together, let no one separate
Do to others as you would have them do to you
Whoever has ears, let them hear
questions.explain: In Mark 10:9 Jesus teaches that marriage is a lifelong bond made by God that should not be broken.

questions.q: In Roman Catholic teaching, marriage is regarded as which of the following?
options: A private agreement with no religious meaning
questions.explain: The Roman Catholic Church teaches that marriage is a sacrament, an outward sign of God's grace.

questions.q: Why do many Christians believe marriage should last for life?
options: Because it is a lifelong covenant reflecting God's faithful love
Because the law forbids all divorce
Because marriage is only about raising children
Because unmarried people cannot attend church
questions.explain: Many Christians see marriage as a lifelong covenant that mirrors God's faithful, unbreakable love.

questions.q: A Catholic couple's marriage has broken down and they want the Church to declare that a valid marriage never existed. What should they seek?
questions.explain: An annulment is the Church's declaration that a true, valid marriage never actually took place.

questions.q: Why does the Roman Catholic Church not permit remarriage after divorce?
options: Because it teaches that marriage is indissoluble
Because divorce is illegal in all countries
Because remarriage requires a second sacrament
questions.explain: The Church holds that a valid marriage cannot be dissolved, so remarriage while a spouse lives is not permitted.

questions.q: In Islam, which term refers to divorce initiated by the husband?
questions.explain: Talaq is the term for divorce pronounced by the husband in Islam.

questions.q: Which teaching reflects the Islamic attitude that divorce, though allowed, is regretted?
options: The most disliked of lawful things to Allah is divorce
Divorce is forbidden in all circumstances
Every Muslim must marry more than once
questions.explain: A hadith teaches that divorce, while permitted, is the most disliked of lawful things to Allah.

questions.q: What is meant by cohabitation?
options: A couple living together as if married without being married
A period of separation before divorce
questions.explain: Cohabitation is when a couple live together in a sexual relationship without being married.

questions.q: Why do many religious believers disapprove of cohabitation?
options: Because it usually involves sex outside marriage
Because it is illegal in the UK
Because it prevents couples from ever marrying
Because it is only practised by non-religious people
questions.explain: Many believers teach that sex belongs only within marriage, so they disapprove of cohabiting relationships.

questions.q: Which Bible verse teaches that 'there is neither male nor female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus'?
questions.explain: Galatians 3:28 is used to support the equal worth of men and women before God.

questions.q: What does a complementarian view of gender roles teach?
options: Men and women have different but complementary God-given roles
Men and women should have identical roles in all things
Women should have no role in family life
Gender roles have no religious significance
questions.explain: A complementarian view holds that men and women are equal in value but have distinct, complementary roles.

questions.q: What is meant by gender equality?
options: Men and women having equal rights, status and opportunities
Only men being allowed to lead worship
questions.explain: Gender equality means men and women are treated as having equal rights, status and opportunities.

questions.q: A church that ordains women as priests and bishops on the same basis as men is best described as holding which view?
questions.explain: An egalitarian view holds that men and women should share the same roles, including leadership, equally.

questions.q: Which of the Ten Commandments directly forbids sex outside marriage between married people?
questions.explain: The commandment 'You shall not commit adultery' forbids sexual unfaithfulness within marriage.

questions.q: In which 1968 papal encyclical did the Roman Catholic Church reaffirm its opposition to artificial contraception?
questions.explain: Humanae Vitae (1968) restated Catholic teaching against the use of artificial contraception.

questions.q: Why does the Roman Catholic Church oppose artificial contraception?
options: Because sex should remain open to the creation of new life
Because it wants families to remain small
questions.explain: The Church teaches that sex within marriage should always be open to procreation, which artificial contraception blocks.

questions.q: Why do many Christians, including the Church of England, accept the use of contraception?
options: To allow responsible family planning within marriage
Because they reject the idea of having children
Because the Bible commands its use
questions.explain: Many Christians accept contraception as a responsible way for married couples to plan their families.

questions.q: A Catholic couple wish to space out the birth of their children while staying faithful to Church teaching. Which method would they use?
questions.explain: The Church permits natural family planning, which works with the body's natural cycle rather than artificial means.

questions.q: After a divorce, a Muslim woman waits a set period before she may remarry, partly to confirm she is not pregnant. What is this period called?
questions.explain: Iddah is the waiting period a Muslim woman observes after divorce or widowhood before she may remarry.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) Religious Studies (J625) specification; Religion, Philosophy & Ethics: Relationships & Families
